# dspevx

> Computes selected eigenvalues and, optionally, eigenvectors of a real.

<section class="intro">

symmetric matrix in packed storage.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dspevx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dspevx';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dspevx(
    order,
    jobz, range, uplo,
    N,
    AP,
    vl, vu, il, iu, abstol,
    m,
    w, strideW,
    Z, LDZ,
    WORK,
    IWORK,
    IFAIL, strideIFAIL
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `jobz` | `("no-vectors"\|"compute-vectors")` | in |  | one of `'no-vectors'`, `'compute-vectors'` | 'no-vectors' or 'compute-vectors' |
| `range` | `("all"\|"value"\|"index")` | in |  | one of `'all'`, `'index'`, `'value'` | 'all', 'value', or 'index' |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | 'upper' or 'lower' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix A |
| `AP` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `trunc( N * (N + 1) / 2 )` |  | packed symmetric matrix (length N*(N+1)/2) |
| `vl` | `number` | in |  |  | lower bound of eigenvalue interval (RANGE='value') |
| `vu` | `number` | in |  | rejects `range === 'value' && (N > 0 && vu <= vl)` | upper bound of eigenvalue interval (RANGE='value') |
| `il` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (il < 1 \|\| il > max( 1, N ))` | index of smallest eigenvalue to compute (1-based, RANGE='index') |
| `iu` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N)` | index of largest eigenvalue to compute (1-based, RANGE='index') |
| `abstol` | `number` | in |  |  | absolute tolerance for eigenvalues |
| `m` | `Int32Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the total number of eigenvalues found |
| `w` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output array for eigenvalues (length N) |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `w` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array` | out | `N × (range === 'index' ? iu - il + 1 : N)` |  | output eigenvector matrix (N x M) |
| ↳ `LDZ` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | rejects `ldz < 1 \|\| (jobz === 'compute-vectors' && ldz < N)` | leading dimension of Z |
| `WORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 8 * N` |  | workspace array (length >= 8*N) |
| `IWORK` | `(Int32Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 5 * N` |  | integer workspace (length >= 5*N) |
| `IFAIL` | `Int32Array` | out | `N` |  | output: indices of non-converged eigenvectors (length N) |
| ↳ `strideIFAIL` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `IFAIL` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `range`:

  -   `= 'A'`: all eigenvalues will be found;
  -   `= 'V'`: all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (`VL`,`VU`\] will be found;
  -   `= 'I'`: the `IL`-th through `IU`-th eigenvalues will be found.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `AP`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the symmetric matrix A, packed columnwise in a linear array. The j-th column of A is stored in the array `AP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = A(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*(2*n-j)/2) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$.

  On exit, `AP` is overwritten by values generated during the reduction to tridiagonal form. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the diagonal and first superdiagonal of the tridiagonal matrix T overwrite the corresponding elements of A, and if `UPLO = 'L'`, the diagonal and first subdiagonal of T overwrite the corresponding elements of A.
- `vl`: If `RANGE='V'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `vu`: If `RANGE='V'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `il`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `iu`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `abstol`: The absolute error tolerance for the eigenvalues. An approximate eigenvalue is accepted as converged when it is determined to lie in an interval \[a,b\] of width less than or equal to

  $$
  \mathrm{ABSTOL} + \mathrm{EPS} \, \max ( |a|,|b| )
  $$

  where EPS is the machine precision. If `ABSTOL` is less than or equal to zero, then EPS\*\|T\| will be used in its place, where \|T\| is the 1-norm of the tridiagonal matrix obtained by reducing `AP` to tridiagonal form.

  Eigenvalues will be computed most accurately when `ABSTOL` is set to twice the underflow threshold $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$, not zero. If this routine returns with $\mathrm{INFO}>0$, indicating that some eigenvectors did not converge, try setting `ABSTOL` to $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$.

  See "Computing Small Singular Values of Bidiagonal Matrices with Guaranteed High Relative Accuracy," by Demmel and Kahan, LAPACK Working Note #3.
- `m`: The total number of eigenvalues found. $0 \le M \le N$. If `RANGE = 'A'`, $M = N$, and if `RANGE = 'I'`, $M = \mathrm{IU}-\mathrm{IL}+1$.
- `w`: If `INFO = 0`, the selected eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `Z`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M columns of Z contain the orthonormal eigenvectors of the matrix A corresponding to the selected eigenvalues, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with `W(i)`. If an eigenvector fails to converge, then that column of Z contains the latest approximation to the eigenvector, and the index of the eigenvector is returned in `IFAIL`. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then Z is not referenced. Note: the user must ensure that at least max(1,M) columns are supplied in the array Z; if `RANGE = 'V'`, the exact value of M is not known in advance and an upper bound must be used.
- `IFAIL`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M elements of `IFAIL` are zero. If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$, then `IFAIL` contains the indices of the eigenvectors that failed to converge. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then `IFAIL` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "all", "index", "value"
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eighth argument is invalid (rejected when `range === "value" && ( N > 0 && vu <= vl )`)
- `RangeError` ninth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( il < 1 \|\| il > max( 1, N ) )`)
- `RangeError` tenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N )`)
- `RangeError` sixteenth argument is invalid (column-major: rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < N )`)
- `RangeError` sixteenth argument is invalid (row-major: rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < max( 1, range === "index" ? iu - il + 1 : N ) )`)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dspevx.ndarray(
    jobz, range, uplo,
    N,
    AP, strideAP, offsetAP,
    vl, vu, il, iu, abstol,
    m,
    w, strideW, offsetW,
    Z, strideZ1, strideZ2, offsetZ,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    IWORK, strideIWork, offsetIWork,
    IFAIL, strideIFAIL, offsetIFAIL
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jobz` | `("no-vectors"\|"compute-vectors")` | in |  | one of `'no-vectors'`, `'compute-vectors'` | 'no-vectors' or 'compute-vectors' |
| `range` | `("all"\|"value"\|"index")` | in |  | one of `'all'`, `'index'`, `'value'` | 'all', 'value', or 'index' |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | 'upper' or 'lower' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix A |
| `AP` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `trunc( N * (N + 1) / 2 )` |  | packed symmetric matrix; on exit, overwritten by dsptrd |
| ↳ `strideAP` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `AP` |
| ↳ `offsetAP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `AP` |
| `vl` | `number` | in |  |  | lower bound of eigenvalue interval (RANGE='value') |
| `vu` | `number` | in |  | rejects `range === 'value' && (N > 0 && vu <= vl)` | upper bound of eigenvalue interval (RANGE='value') |
| `il` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (il < 1 \|\| il > max( 1, N ))` | index of smallest eigenvalue to compute (1-based, RANGE='index') |
| `iu` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N)` | index of largest eigenvalue to compute (1-based, RANGE='index') |
| `abstol` | `number` | in |  |  | absolute tolerance for eigenvalues |
| `m` | `Int32Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the total number of eigenvalues found |
| `w` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output array for eigenvalues (length N) |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `w` |
| ↳ `offsetW` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `w` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array` | out | `N × (range === 'index' ? iu - il + 1 : N)` |  | output eigenvector matrix (N x M) |
| ↳ `strideZ1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of first dimension of `Z` |
| ↳ `strideZ2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of second dimension of `Z` |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `Z` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ 8 * N` |  | workspace (length >= 8*N) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `WORK` |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array` | out | `≥ 5 * N` |  | integer workspace (length >= 5*N) |
| ↳ `strideIWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `IWORK` |
| ↳ `offsetIWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `IWORK` |
| `IFAIL` | `Int32Array` | out | `N` |  | output: indices of non-converged eigenvectors (length N) |
| ↳ `strideIFAIL` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `IFAIL` |
| ↳ `offsetIFAIL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `IFAIL` |

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "all", "index", "value"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` ninth argument is invalid (rejected when `range === "value" && ( N > 0 && vu <= vl )`)
- `RangeError` tenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( il < 1 \|\| il > max( 1, N ) )`)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N )`)
- `RangeError` `IWORK` must have at least `5 * N` elements from `offsetIWork`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, then i eigenvectors failed to converge. Their indices are stored in array `IFAIL`.

## Notes

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dspevx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dspevx';

// 3x3 symmetric [[2,1,0],[1,3,1],[0,1,4]] upper packed:
const m = new Int32Array( 1 );

const AP = new Float64Array( [ 2.0, 1.0, 3.0, 0.0, 1.0, 4.0 ] );
const w = new Float64Array( 3 );
const Z = new Float64Array( 9 );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 24 );
const IWORK = new Int32Array( 15 );
const IFAIL = new Int32Array( 3 );

dspevx.ndarray( 'compute-vectors', 'all', 'upper', 3, AP, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, m, w, 1, 0, Z, 1, 3, 0, WORK, 1, 0, IWORK, 1, 0, IFAIL, 1, 0 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'Number of eigenvalues found: %d', m[ 0 ] );
console.log( 'Eigenvalues:', w );
console.log( 'Eigenvectors (column-major):', Z );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DSPEVX`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DSPEVX computes selected eigenvalues and, optionally, eigenvectors of a real symmetric matrix A in packed storage. Eigenvalues/vectors can be selected by specifying either a range of values or a range of indices for the desired eigenvalues.

</section>
